findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify or drop the two `criteria_routing.json` blast-radius entries: reconcile with the ADR-0053 regver stamp that already binds effective routing as deliberately-non-blocking `registry_drift`, and state why blocking invalidation is warranted here.
evidence: manifest.py:131-135 `_routing_stamp` docstring: 'the stamp hashes the repo's EFFECTIVE routing (packaged ⊕ the .rebar/criteria_routing.json overlay)' and 'Since ADR 0053 a rotated stamp is GRANDFATHERED at the claim gate: it is reported as non-blocking registry_drift rather than invalidating a prior plan-review attestation'
manifest.py:153 `routing = json.dumps(routing_obj, sort_keys=True)` feeds the regver basis
Plan (b): a touched blast-radius path 'invalidates' — the opposite of the grandfathered regver semantics
findings.finding: The blast-radius set hardcodes `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`, but effective routing (packaged overlay + `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`) is ALREADY bound into the signed `regver` stamp — which ADR 0053 deliberately GRANDFATHERS as non-blocking `registry_drift` at the claim gate. Adding these paths as blast-radius dep entries would make routing drift INVALIDATE no-file_impact attestations, re-litigating a dimension the codebase intentionally made non-blocking, via a second overlapping mechanism.
scenarios: A project re-tunes .rebar/criteria_routing.json: today this is a non-blocking regver rotation, but a no-file_impact ticket would now be invalidated by the blast-radius membership digest / per-file hash.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly whether read-set scoping applies to file_impact_scope=='none' (authenticated no-impact, today fully exempt) as well as 'undeclared', and reconcile with classify_file_scope (which reclassifies any non-empty dep set to 'paths') so the exemption is not silently removed.
evidence: Plan (b): 'For a ticket with **no** `file_impact` whose manifest carries a recorded read-set, `dependency_hashes` composes read-set ∪ cited paths ∪ expanded blast-radius'
attest.py L585: `elif manifest_file_scope(auth_manifest) != "none"` — a signed file-scope: none authenticated no-impact attestation currently SKIPS all code-drift checks
manifest.py L359: `if any(dependency_paths): return "paths"` — any composed dep entry (blast-radius globs always exist) reclassifies the ticket to 'paths'
Codebase separates three scopes (undeclared/paths/none) — docs/ticket-model.md L210-212, reducer _state.py
findings.finding: The plan's scoping trigger 'a ticket with no file_impact' does not distinguish the codebase's two empty-file_impact scopes — 'undeclared' (today: whole-HEAD invalidate-on-any-change, the over-trigger being fixed) vs authenticated 'none' (today: FULLY EXEMPT from code drift via the file_scope=='none' skip at attest.py L585). Composing read-set ∪ cited ∪ blast-radius yields a non-empty dep set, which classify_file_scope (manifest.py L359) reclassifies from 'none' to 'paths', so a previously-exempt authenticated-no-impact attestation would newly invalidate whenever a read-set or blast-radius file drifts.
findings.location: Section (b) 'For a ticket with no file_impact whose manifest carries a recorded read-set…'; interacts with attest.py compute_validity L585 and manifest.classify_file_scope L355-363
scenarios: A ticket declares file_impact_scope: none with a substantive no_file_impact_reason (a doc-only or evidence-only ticket) and was reviewed with an agentic pass that recorded a read-set; a later commit touches a blast-radius file (e.g. rebar.toml or a criteria_routing.json overlay), invalidating a currency check that was previously fully exempt.
Conversely, if the intent is to leave 'none'-declared tickets exempt, an implementer reading 'no file_impact' literally would wrongly apply scoping to them.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope (b) to the 'undeclared' fail-safe only (the case that today falls through to whole-HEAD invalidate), and preserve the authenticated file_impact_scope=='none' exemption unchanged — e.g. only compose read-set/blast-radius when the signed file_scope would otherwise be 'unscoped', and keep emitting file-scope: none for authenticated-none tickets so the L585 skip still applies.

findings.finding: The blast-radius glob list hardcodes `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`, but both files are already bound into the same signed manifest via the existing `regver:` stamp (registry_version hashes the EFFECTIVE routing = packaged routing + the overlay). This is an overlapping/duplicate invalidation surface for the same two files, and the two mechanisms disagree on outcome: a routing edit invalidates as grandfathered non-blocking `registry_drift` (ADR 0053) via regver, but as hard `stale-code` via the new dep entry. The plan does not reconcile the overlap or the conflicting severity.
findings.location: Section (b), 'Blast-radius entries' list; cross-ref manifest.py:125-171 (registry_version) and manifest.py:437 (dep lines)
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` from the blast-radius list (both are already bound via regver) and keep only the entries regver does not cover: criteria/**, reviewers/*.md, gates/*.yaml, plus rebar.toml. Add a one-line note that routing JSONs are covered by the regver stamp, not the dep set.

findings.finding: Section (b) claims the membership digest 'closes the addition/deletion blind spot' and that a deleted member 'moves both it and (via _ABSENT_HASH) its own entry', but AC2 only exercises a file ADDED under a glob. No acceptance criterion exercises deletion of a glob member, so the deletion half of the claimed capability is unmeasured.
findings.location: Section (b) 'This closes the addition/deletion blind spot' vs Acceptance Criteria bullet 2

evidence: 4 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: Section (b) states 'compute_validity's per-path re-hash loop is unchanged' yet later says compute_validity/_rehash both call the new hash_dep_entry helper (dispatching glob patterns to a membership digest). The re-hash step is in fact changed — it must now dispatch per entry rather than call _hash_file directly.
findings.location: Section (b), 'compute_validity's per-path re-hash loop is unchanged' vs 'Signing ... and the claim-gate re-check (compute_validity, _rehash) both call it'
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'the re-hash loop is unchanged' to 'the re-hash loop's iteration is unchanged, but each entry is now hashed via hash_dep_entry, which dispatches glob patterns to the membership digest'.

findings.finding: The plan names `hash_dep_entry` callers as `dependency_hashes` and `compute_validity`/`_rehash`, but `compute_validity`'s DEFAULT claim-gate re-hash loop calls `_hash_file` INLINE (attest.py:575), not `_rehash` — yet the plan also states that loop 'is unchanged'. These two claims contradict: for a glob PATTERN dep entry (membership digest) to re-verify, the inline `_hash_file(p, base=base)` at attest.py:575 must itself dispatch through `hash_dep_entry`, otherwise the pattern is hashed as a literal filename to `_ABSENT_HASH` and mismatches the signed membership digest on every claim, invalidating unconditionally.
findings.location: Section (b), 'Both sides route through ONE helper …' and 'compute_validity's per-path re-hash loop is unchanged'
findings.suggested_fix: State that the claim-gate DEFAULT loop in compute_validity (attest.py:568-576) is changed to call `read_set.hash_dep_entry(p, base=base)` instead of `_hash_file(p, base=base)`, and that `_rehash` (attest.py:204) is likewise routed through it so the drift_refresh/refresh_attestation paths agree; drop the 'is unchanged' wording.

findings.finding: The patch-site inventory for routing hashing through the new hash_dep_entry helper omits (and contradicts itself on) compute_validity's DEFAULT-profile drift loop at attest.py:575. That loop calls _hash_file(p, base=base) directly, not _rehash; the plan names compute_validity as a hash_dep_entry caller yet also declares its per-path loop 'unchanged.' Since _hash_file returns _ABSENT_HASH for any non-openable path (manifest.py:184-185), a recorded glob-PATTERN membership-digest line handled by the unchanged loop mismatches the signed digest on every check.
findings.location: Section (b), 'Both sides route through ONE helper … Signing (dependency_hashes) and the claim-gate re-check (compute_validity, _rehash) both call it' vs. 'compute_validity's per-path re-hash loop is unchanged — it still iterates the concrete recorded entries.'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the `_hash_file(p, base=base)` call in the compute_validity DEFAULT drift loop (attest.py:575) with `hash_dep_entry(p, base=base)`, and enumerate all _hash_file re-hash sites converted (attest.py:575, _rehash at attest.py:208) so the loop dispatching on glob metacharacters matches signing.
